title: Gabriel in-laws and the Gabriel trio
summary: Marrying into the Gabriel musical family drew him into music; he describes the family and the banjo, bass and clarinet trio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was your cousin's name, the Clarinet player?

You called him Dude. Dude. Yeah, he was formerly from Algiers. Well, he wasn't exactly my cousin. He was my wife's cousin. You see. And, but when I met up with my wife, and the family, her family, she played piano. And her daddy played trumpet. Her brother was a drummer at that time. Well, now he's playing saxophone. He don't live there. He's a little drummer. And the rest of them, well, they were too small. But I have a brother in law. He plays piano. He used to play band jazz. But you know, we played with Louis DeMaine.
And just by getting into that family, that's how I started on that music.
What was your wife's father's name? Gabriel.
Well, he was, there were all that big...

The trumpet, that's the one on that picture there. The trumpet player. Yeah. He had the national jazz office right at that time. Around 1918, up until about 1920, well, around 1930, I think he was still playing.
We used to play with him, and then we played with others. Then there was two brothers and myself who formed a trio. We played all around. Trials? Trials was, wasn't famous. We had a trio.
What did you, what are your instruments?
Banjo, bass, and clarinet. Oh, that's... You played the bass at that time? Yeah, we played at Victors out here. Oh yeah. On, I think it was the charter and tools. Yeah, still there.
